capture_contract.classification: deterministic masked derivative of native stdout/stderr
capture_contract.rule: Replace the exact privately supplied scratch root with <PRIVATE_SCRATCH_ROOT>, then Unix/macOS private home-path and UUID tokens; preserve every other byte, including failures, ANSI, timestamps and line breaks. No summaries or synthetic output substitute for a native capture.
capture_contract.raw_custody: Private captures are referenced by basename only; co-op privately replays the published mask. Only published derivative hashes appear here.
capture_contract.command_paths: /work and /runtime are real paths inside the isolated namespaces. Host mount-source paths are marked <PRIVATE_SCRATCH_ROOT>, <PRIVATE_NODE_RUNTIME>, <PRIVATE_VLLM_PREFIX>, <PRIVATE_PYTHON_RUNTIME> in reproduction notes; exact wrapper is held privately as capture-native.py.

attempt_disclosure.recaptured_results: All relied-on numeric/native results above were recaptured directly after integrity addendum-01; earlier excerpt-only draft receipts were discarded.
attempt_disclosure.missing_captures: Earlier npm sandbox-home/config/localhost setup attempts and first generic-platform resolver attempt have no compliant original raw capture in this packet. They remain named preparation gaps/history, never evidence of candidate behavior.
attempt_disclosure.retained_failed_integration: The first offline integration failed before tests when Qdrant could not load CA roots. Its raw streams are retained; retry adds read-only public CA roots while keeping the network namespace isolated.
attempt_disclosure.scratch_state: The successful retry reused owned scratch storage and loaded the first attempt's raft state (captures/qdrant-offline.stdout:14). New process/network namespace, not a fresh data directory.

isolation.cleanup: offline-integration.sh trap signals/waits only for its owned PID; namespace teardown removes access to the owned process.
isolation.fence: No GPU devices, broker/account actions or credential/config mounts.
